explanation: secOpsOutput_94 is written by /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_94 (NOT configdrift.sh, contrary to earlier versions of this entry -- that attribution has been retracted after reading secOpsScript_94's real source, 2026-08-28). It's the PRIMARY and ONLY evidence for the config_drift attack type -- secOpsScript_94 never writes any Alert.xml or alertlog.xml tag, so this file's own content is the ground truth, not a secondary snapshot to diff against something else. Format: alternating line pairs -- a tracked item's name, then its status ('None' = clean, 'Tampered' = drift detected) on the next line. Tracked items are: each admin-configured path from ConfigDriftControl.xml's driftpath_N entries (e.g. rclient_config.xml, MetricBinLogs.xml), plus two fixed checks always appended -- 'FirewallStatus' (unexpected open ports) and 'IdentityAsset' (identity-asset mapping drift, via identity_assets_mapping.py). A 'Tampered' item only appears after its underlying diff persisted past a 24-hour grace window since the reference/install time -- a change caught within that window silently becomes the new baseline instead of being flagged.
